docs.title: go-pkcs7
docs.text:
go-pkcs7 is a Go library that parses and builds the parts of the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS, RFC 5652) that certificate enrollment protocols use. SCEP (RFC 8894) wraps every request and response in these messages. go-pki-scep is built on this library.

It handles three content types:

  • SignedData: signing with RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 or ECDSA keys and verification of RSA PKCS #1 v1.5, RSASSA-PSS (RFC 4055) and ECDSA signatures. Content may be attached or detached and a message may have several signers or carry only certificates or a CRL.
  • EnvelopedData: content encrypted for RSA recipient certificates with PKCS #1 v1.5 or RSAES-OAEP (RFC 8017) key transport.
  • EncryptedData: content encrypted with a pre-shared key.

Algorithm choices are made per call through option structs, so two parts of one program can apply different policies. Signing keys are crypto.Signer and decryption keys crypto.Decrypter values, so they may live in an HSM. Input may be BER or DER. The module needs Go 1.27.3 or newer and has no dependencies outside the standard library.

docs.text:
go-pkcs7 continues the work of these projects and their contributors:

  • fullsailor/pkcs7, the original implementation by Andrew Smith.
  • mozilla-services/pkcs7, the Mozilla fork.

All three are MIT licensed. NOTICE records the origins of the code, including the copies of Go 1.23 crypto/x509 and golang.org/x/crypto/cryptobyte under internal/.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This page adds the module to a project, signs and verifies a message and encrypts content for a recipient certificate.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
go get github.com/misiektoja/go-pkcs7

The module needs Go 1.27.3 or newer and has no dependencies outside the standard library. The package is imported as pkcs7:

import "github.com/misiektoja/go-pkcs7"

The API may still change before v1.0.0, as the Compatibility policy describes.

docs.title: Sign and verify
docs.text:
NewSignedData starts a message over the content. AddSigner signs it with the signer certificate cert and its private key key, an RSA or ECDSA crypto.Signer. Finish returns the encoded message:

sd, err := pkcs7.NewSignedData([]byte("hello, CMS"))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := sd.AddSigner(cert, key, pkcs7.SignerInfoConfig{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
signed, err := sd.Finish()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

The receiver parses the message and verifies it against the CA certificate it trusts:

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(signed)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
roots := x509.NewCertPool()
roots.AddCert(caCert)
if err := p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{Roots: roots}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("%s\n", p7.Content)

Verify checks the message digest, the signed attributes and the signature of every signer. With Roots set it also builds a chain from each signer certificate to one of the roots. Without Roots it checks the signatures only, so the caller must decide whether to trust the signer. Verification covers the options.

docs.title: Encrypt and decrypt
docs.text:
Encrypt creates an EnvelopedData message for one or more RSA recipient certificates:

enveloped, err := pkcs7.Encrypt([]byte("for the recipient only"), []*x509.Certificate{recipientCert}, pkcs7.EncryptOptions{
    ContentEncryption: pkcs7.AES256CBC,
    KeyEncryption:     pkcs7.RSAOAEP,
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

The recipient decrypts it with its certificate and private key:

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(enveloped)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
plaintext, err := p7.Decrypt(recipientCert, recipientKey, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("%s\n", plaintext)

The defaults are AES-128-CBC and PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport, which SCEP peers expect. This example selects AES-256-CBC and RSAES-OAEP instead. Encryption and decryption explains the choices.

docs.title: Run the examples
docs.text:
Apart from the import line above, the Go listings on this site come from example_test.go in the repository, where each one runs as a Go example and checks its output. Run them from a clone:

go test -run Example -v .

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Support matrix lists the algorithms and message forms.
  • Security model explains what Verify and Decrypt guarantee and what they leave to the caller.
  • Known limitations lists what is not supported.

docs.title: Content types
docs.text:
• No AuthEnvelopedData (RFC 5083) and no AES-GCM. Parse returns ErrUnsupportedContentType for AuthEnvelopedData, which is what openssl cms -encrypt -aes-128-gcm produces.
  • No DigestedData, AuthenticatedData or other content types. Parse returns ErrUnsupportedContentType.
  • Signing always uses the id-data content type. Messages with another encapsulated content type can be parsed and verified but not created.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
• Signing supports RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 and ECDSA only. No RSASSA-PSS, Ed25519, DSA or post-quantum signing.
  • Verification supports RSA PKCS #1 v1.5, RSASSA-PSS and ECDSA. Ed25519 and DSA signatures fail. An ECDSA signature with SHA-224 fails unless the signature algorithm field names the curve.
  • Signers are identified by issuer and serial number. Parse fails on a signer identified by subject key identifier, which is what openssl cms -sign -keyid produces.
  • No countersignatures, signed receipts or timestamps. Unsigned attributes can be added but are not interpreted.
  • No revocation checking. Verify does not consult CRLs or OCSP. CRLs carried in a message are not checked either.

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
• Recipients must hold RSA keys. No key agreement (ECDH), key encryption key or password recipients. Encrypt refuses other keys with ErrUnsupportedKeyType. Parse fails on a message that contains such a recipient, even when another recipient uses RSA.
  • Recipients are identified by issuer and serial number. Parse fails on a recipient identified by subject key identifier, which openssl cms -encrypt -keyid produces.
  • CBC content is not authenticated. A changed ciphertext or a wrong key can decrypt to garbage instead of failing. Sign the message when integrity matters.
  • No key derivation for pre-shared keys. EncryptUsingPSK takes raw key bytes.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• No streaming. Messages are held in memory while they are parsed or built. The library does not limit their size.
  • DegenerateCertificate does not parse its input. It wraps whatever bytes it receives.
  • Embedded certificates must parse with crypto/x509. The only exception is a critical authority key identifier with ParseOptions.LegacyCertificateParser.

docs.title: Migrating from smallstep/pkcs7
docs.text: go-pkcs7 started from smallstep/pkcs7 v0.2.3. The package name is still pkcs7, but the module path, several signatures and some defaults changed. This page lists what code written for smallstep/pkcs7 needs. The changelog for 0.3.0 has the full list.

docs.title: Module path
docs.text:
Replace the import path github.com/smallstep/pkcs7 with github.com/misiektoja/go-pkcs7 and run:

go get github.com/misiektoja/go-pkcs7

The module needs Go 1.27.3 or newer.

docs.title: API changes
docs.text:
These changes stop the old code from compiling:

smallstep/pkcs7 go-pkcs7 p7.Verify() p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{}) p7.VerifyWithChain(roots) p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{Roots: roots}), see Chain time p7.VerifyWithChainAtTime(roots, t) p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{Roots: roots, CurrentTime: t}) pkcs7.Encrypt(content, recipients) pkcs7.Encrypt(content, recipients, pkcs7.EncryptOptions{}) pkcs7.EncryptUsingPSK(content, key) pkcs7.EncryptUsingPSK(content, key, pkcs7.EncryptOptions{}) p7.Decrypt(cert, privateKey) p7.Decrypt(cert, key, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{}) p7.DecryptUsingPSK(key) p7.DecryptUsingPSK(key, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{}) pkcs7.ContentEncryptionAlgorithm = ... EncryptOptions.ContentEncryption pkcs7.KeyEncryptionAlgorithm = ... EncryptOptions.KeyEncryption, such as pkcs7.RSAOAEP pkcs7.KeyEncryptionHash = ... EncryptOptions.OAEPHash pkcs7.SetDefaultDigestAlgorithm(oid) sd.SetDigestAlgorithm(oid) on each SignedData pkcs7.SetFallbackLegacyX509CertificateParserEnabled(true) pkcs7.ParseWithOptions(data, pkcs7.ParseOptions{LegacyCertificateParser: true}) pkcs7.EncryptionAlgorithmDESCBC, EncryptionAlgorithmAES128CBC, EncryptionAlgorithmAES256CBC pkcs7.DESCBC, pkcs7.AES128CBC, pkcs7.AES256CBC pkcs7.EncryptionAlgorithmAES128GCM, EncryptionAlgorithmAES256GCM Removed, see Removed features OIDDigestAlgorithmDSA, OIDDigestAlgorithmDSASHA1, OIDEncryptionAlgorithmAES128GCM, OIDEncryptionAlgorithmAES256GCM Removed

AddSigner, AddSignerChain and SignWithoutAttr take a crypto.Signer and Decrypt takes a crypto.Decrypter instead of crypto.PrivateKey. *rsa.PrivateKey is both and *ecdsa.PrivateKey is a crypto.Signer, so code that passes them keeps compiling unless it holds the key in a crypto.PrivateKey variable. A type assertion fixes that. *dsa.PrivateKey is not a crypto.Signer, so code that signs with a DSA key no longer compiles.

docs.title: Changed defaults
docs.text:
These changes compile without errors but change the messages:

Setting smallstep/pkcs7 go-pkcs7 Signing digest SHA-1 SHA-256 Content cipher for Encrypt and EncryptUsingPSK DES-CBC AES-128-CBC Content ciphers Decrypt and DecryptUsingPSK accept All implemented AES-CBC and DES-EDE3-CBC. DES-CBC must be listed in DecryptOptions

A peer that only understands the old defaults needs them set explicitly, through SetDigestAlgorithm(pkcs7.OIDDigestAlgorithmSHA1) or EncryptOptions{ContentEncryption: pkcs7.DESCBC}.

docs.title: Chain time
docs.text: VerifyWithChain checked the chain at the time in the signing-time attribute. Without that attribute it used the current time. Verify with Roots checks it at the current time. Set VerifyAtSigningTime to keep the old behavior for archived signatures, after reading Check time.

docs.title: Stricter checks
docs.text:
Messages that smallstep/pkcs7 accepted may now fail:

  • Signed attributes must contain exactly one message-digest attribute and exactly one content-type attribute. The content type must equal the encapsulated content type.
  • A digest algorithm field holding rsaEncryption or an ECDSA signature identifier is no longer read as a digest. RSA signature identifiers such as sha256WithRSAEncryption there are still accepted.
  • Malformed BER, nesting deeper than 64 levels and trailing data after the message are refused.
  • Decrypt returns ErrDecryptionFailed for every key or padding failure instead of a specific error.

The texts of several error variables changed, including ErrNotEncryptedContent and ErrUnsupportedAlgorithm. Compare errors with errors.Is.

docs.title: New features
docs.text: MD5 and SHA-224 digests, RSASSA-PSS verification, AES-192-CBC, encryption with DES-EDE3-CBC, AES-CBC for EncryptUsingPSK, VerifyOptions with intermediates, signer certificates and key usages, Recipients, ContentEncryptionAlgorithm, DegenerateCRL, RemoveCertificates and SignerInfoConfig.SigningTime are new. RSAES-OAEP with a hash other than SHA-1 now names the matching MGF1 hash, so OpenSSL can decrypt it.

docs.title: Removed features
docs.text:
• AES-GCM. The encoding smallstep/pkcs7 used did not follow RFC 5084, so its GCM messages cannot be decrypted here. Use AES-CBC.
  • DSA. Signing with *dsa.PrivateKey and verifying DSA signatures are no longer supported.

docs.title: Content types
docs.text:
Content type Create Read SignedData (RFC 5652 section 5) NewSignedData, DegenerateCertificate and DegenerateCRL Parse, then Verify EnvelopedData (RFC 5652 section 6) Encrypt Parse, then Decrypt EncryptedData (RFC 5652 section 8) EncryptUsingPSK Parse, then DecryptUsingPSK

Parse returns ErrUnsupportedContentType for every other content type, including DigestedData, AuthenticatedData and AuthEnvelopedData (RFC 5083).

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
Algorithm Signing Verification RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 The same digests. MD5 only with VerifyOptions.AllowMD5 RSASSA-PSS (RFC 4055) No SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 with explicit parameters ECDSA SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 The same digests Ed25519, DSA and others No No

Signing uses SHA-256 unless SetDigestAlgorithm selects another digest. The tests sign and verify with RSA keys of 2048, 3072 and 4096 bits and ECDSA keys on P-256, P-384 and P-521.

The signature algorithm identifier written for a signer is sha256WithRSAEncryption or ecdsa-with-SHA256 for the default digest. SetEncryptionAlgorithm(OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSA) writes rsaEncryption instead for RSA signers. Verification accepts both forms for RSA. For ECDSA it also accepts a curve identifier in place of the signature algorithm, which some signers write. That form works with any supported digest. Algorithms lists every identifier.

docs.title: Key transport
docs.text:
EnvelopedData recipients are RSA certificates identified by issuer and serial number.

Key transport Encrypt Decrypt RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5 Yes, the default Yes, with the RFC 3218 countermeasure RSAES-OAEP (RFC 8017) SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 for the hash and MGF1, SHA-256 by default The same hashes. The OAEP hash and the MGF1 hash may differ and a label is accepted

Recipients identified by subject key identifier, key agreement (ECDH), key encryption key and password recipients are not supported. Parse fails on a message that contains one.

docs.title: Content ciphers
docs.text:
Constant Cipher Key Encrypt Decrypt by default AES128CBC AES-128-CBC 16 bytes Yes, the default Yes AES192CBC AES-192-CBC 24 bytes Yes Yes AES256CBC AES-256-CBC 32 bytes Yes Yes DESEDE3CBC DES-EDE3-CBC 24 bytes Yes Yes DESCBC DES-CBC 8 bytes Yes No, it must be listed in DecryptOptions

The same ciphers apply to EnvelopedData and EncryptedData. AES-GCM and other authenticated modes are not supported.

docs.title: Message forms
docs.text: Form Supported Attached content Yes Detached content Yes, Detach when signing and p7.Content when verifying Several signers Yes, each with its own digest algorithm Signer without signed attributes Yes, SignWithoutAttr Signer certificate left out of the message Yes, RemoveCertificates when signing and VerifyOptions.SignerCertificates when verifying Certificates only, the form of a .p7b file Yes, DegenerateCertificate One CRL only, the form of a SCEP GetCRL response Yes, DegenerateCRL Encapsulated content type other than id-data Read and verify only. Signing always uses id-data Countersignatures and signed receipts No

docs.title: Encodings
docs.text:
Parse accepts BER and DER. Indefinite lengths are converted to definite ones and constructed OCTET STRINGs that hold the content are joined. PEM is not read directly: decode it with encoding/pem first, as Parsing shows.

The library writes definite lengths and sorts signed and unsigned attributes as DER requires. Its output is not always strict DER:

  • Certificates are written in the order they were added, not sorted.
  • DegenerateCertificate copies its input bytes without parsing them.
  • RSAES-OAEP parameters with SHA-1 spell out the SHA-1 default instead of omitting it.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: CI builds and tests the module on Linux and macOS and builds it on Windows, with the Go version go.mod declares. The tests that call OpenSSL run where openssl is on the PATH.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: How to build, check and change the library. Contribution rules are in CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go at the version go.mod declares. Go downloads that toolchain on first use when the installed version is older.
  • openssl on the PATH for the interoperability tests. Without it they skip.
  • Python 3 with the pinned MkDocs dependencies for the documentation site, installed by make docs-deps. CI uses Python 3.13.

Linters and other tools are downloaded into bin/ at pinned versions by the Make targets that need them.

docs.title: Common commands
docs.text:
make fmt-check     # fail when a tracked Go file is not gofmt formatted
make test          # go vet and the tests under the race detector
make lint          # golangci-lint at the version CI uses
make fuzz          # each fuzz target for FUZZTIME, 30s by default
make actionlint    # lint the GitHub Actions workflows
make docs-build    # strict MkDocs build
make help          # every target

make tidy-check fails when go.mod is not tidy. make govulncheck reports known vulnerabilities that reach the code and make gitleaks scans the tree and the history for credentials.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs and the Material theme from docs/ and mkdocs.yml. Set PYTHON when the MkDocs toolchain lives in a virtual environment:

make docs-deps PYTHON=.venv/bin/python
make docs-serve PYTHON=.venv/bin/python

make docs-build runs with --strict, so a broken link, a missing anchor or a page absent from the navigation fails the build. CI runs the same build on every change to the documentation and publishes the site from main. The build job holds a read-only token and hands the site to a separate publish job, so the only job that can write to the repository runs no code from PyPI or from the checkout.

The Go listings on the site are named sections of example_test.go, which the pymdownx.snippets extension includes by file and section name. Start and end marker comments delimit each section. Each listing belongs to an example with an // Output: comment, so make test fails when a listing stops compiling or its output changes. Keep a blank line between the end marker and the // Output: comment, because Go reads the expected output only from a comment group that starts with it.

docs/requirements.txt pins every package, including the transitive ones, by version and SHA-256 hash. make docs-deps installs it with --require-hashes. To change a direct dependency, edit docs/requirements.in and run make docs-requirements, which needs pip-tools in the PYTHON environment.

Package documentation on pkg.go.dev comes from the Go doc comments. A user-facing change updates both.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text: .editorconfig records the whitespace rules. gofmt and golangci-lint enforce the rest. A change to a message format cites the RFC section and comes with a negative test.

docs.title: Release process
docs.text: A release starts when a version tag reachable from main is pushed. CHANGELOG.md has one section per version. That section becomes the release description.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The module follows semantic versioning under the Compatibility policy. Clones made from smallstep/pkcs7 hold its tags up to v0.2.3. Those tags declare the old module path, so go get cannot fetch them under this one. Number releases above them so a tag never names two different trees. Push only the new tag.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. On dev, complete the ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD section in CHANGELOG.md and read it as a user of the library.

  2. Merge dev into main and run the checks there:

    make fmt-check
make lint
make test
VERSION=vX.Y.Z make release-check

    The release check fails when go.mod has a replace directive. It exports HEAD with git archive and verifies, builds, vets and tests the export. It then imports the export from a separate module, so it catches files that are ignored, untracked or only present locally. With VERSION set it also requires a dated changelog heading for the version and no Unreleased section.

  3. Create a signed annotated tag and push main and the tag:

    git tag -s vX.Y.Z -m 'vX.Y.Z'
git push origin main vX.Y.Z

  4. The release workflow checks that the tag is reachable from the default branch, repeats the release check, builds the source archives, the SBOM and the checksums, attests their provenance and creates a draft release with the changelog section as its description. Review the draft and publish it.

Never publish a release in the GitHub UI

Publishing there creates the tag, which starts the workflow against a release that is already published. The workflow refuses to rebuild it. Delete the release and its tag with gh release delete vX.Y.Z --cleanup-tag --yes, then push the tag again.

When a draft release for the version already exists, the workflow updates that draft with the changelog section and the artifacts instead of creating a new one.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
Each release carries:

Artifact Content go-pkcs7-<version>-source.zip and .tar.gz The complete tagged source tree go-pkcs7-<version>-sbom.cdx.json A CycloneDX software bill of materials with license information go-pkcs7-<version>_SHA256SUMS.txt SHA-256 checksums of the archives and the SBOM go-pkcs7-<version>.intoto.jsonl A signed provenance bundle covering the artifacts

Verify a file with gh attestation verify <file> --repo misiektoja/go-pkcs7. Offline verification takes --bundle and the provenance file.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: The documentation workflow publishes this site from main to GitHub Pages whenever the pages, mkdocs.yml, example_test.go, the Makefile or the workflow file change there. A manual run on main publishes too. Pull requests, pushes to dev and manual runs on other branches run the strict build without publishing. The site therefore describes main, which is the latest release plus any fixes merged since.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: The library is tested with unit tests, examples, recorded messages from other software, OpenSSL and fuzzing. This page explains how to run each and what it covers.

docs.title: Unit tests and examples
docs.text:
make test

Runs go vet and every test under the race detector. TESTFLAGS passes extra flags, for example make test TESTFLAGS=-v to see which tests skipped. The tests cover:

  • signing and verification with RSA and ECDSA signers through root, intermediate and signer chains, attached and detached, with several digests
  • the signed attribute rules, signing time checks, VerifyOptions and RSASSA-PSS parameters
  • encryption and decryption with every content cipher and key transport, padding errors and the inputs Decrypt must refuse without saying why
  • the BER converter, including indefinite lengths and the limits on hostile input

The examples in example_test.go run as part of the same suite and compare their output with the // Output: comments. They are the code shown on this site.

docs.title: Recorded messages
docs.text:
Several tests read messages that other software produced. The TestParse tests only parse them. The others also verify them:

Test Message TestVerifyAppStore An Apple App Store receipt TestParseSignedOctetStringWithAppleAttestation An Apple App Attest receipt in BER with its content split into several OCTET STRINGs TestVerifyApkEcdsa A detached ECDSA signature from an Android APK TestVerifyFirefoxAddon A Firefox add-on signature, checked at the signing time and at fixed times TestAzureAttestationSignatureValidation An Azure instance metadata attested data document with an RSA signature identifier in the digest field TestParseWindowsSCEPCertificateRequest A Windows SCEP request whose certificate needs LegacyCertificateParser

docs.title: OpenSSL
docs.text:
The OpenSSL tests run with the regular suite when openssl is on the PATH and skip otherwise. OpenSSL lists the commands and what each test checks. To run only them:

go test -count=1 -run 'OpenSSL|TestDegenerate' -v .

docs.title: Fuzzing
docs.text:
make fuzz
make fuzz FUZZTIME=2m

Runs FuzzBer2Der and FuzzParse for FUZZTIME each, 30 seconds by default. FuzzBer2Der checks that the converter never panics and that converting its output again changes nothing. FuzzParse checks that parsing, verification and decryption of arbitrary input return errors instead of panicking. CI runs both on Linux for 30 seconds on every push and pull request to dev and main.

Go writes a failing input under testdata/fuzz/<target>. Commit it with the fix so it stays a regression test.

docs.title: Encryption and decryption
docs.text: An EnvelopedData message carries content encrypted with a random content key and that key encrypted once for each recipient. This library supports recipients with RSA certificates.

docs.title: Encrypt for a recipient
docs.text:
enveloped, err := pkcs7.Encrypt([]byte("for the recipient only"), []*x509.Certificate{recipientCert}, pkcs7.EncryptOptions{
    ContentEncryption: pkcs7.AES256CBC,
    KeyEncryption:     pkcs7.RSAOAEP,
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

Encrypt generates a content key and an IV, encrypts the content in CBC mode with PKCS #7 padding and encrypts the content key for every certificate in the list. Each recipient is identified by the issuer and serial number of its certificate.

Encrypt fails with pkcs7: no recipients for an empty list and with ErrUnsupportedKeyType when a certificate does not hold an RSA key. It does not check the validity period or the key usage of the certificates, so check them before encrypting.

docs.title: Choosing the algorithms
docs.text:
EncryptOptions selects the content cipher and the key transport:

Field Default Choices ContentEncryption AES128CBC AES128CBC, AES192CBC, AES256CBC, DESEDE3CBC and DESCBC KeyEncryption RSAPKCS1v15 RSAPKCS1v15 and RSAOAEP OAEPHash SHA-256 SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. Used only with RSAOAEP

AES-128-CBC with PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport is the default because SCEP peers expect it. Use AES-256-CBC and RSAES-OAEP when the receiver supports them. RSAES-OAEP uses OAEPHash for both the OAEP hash and MGF1. The parameters name both hashes explicitly and carry no label, which OpenSSL reads correctly.

A responder that answers in the cipher the requester chose reads it with ContentEncryptionAlgorithm:

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(request)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
alg, err := p7.ContentEncryptionAlgorithm()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
reply, err := pkcs7.Encrypt([]byte("reply"), []*x509.Certificate{clientCert}, pkcs7.EncryptOptions{ContentEncryption: alg})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println("reply encrypted with", alg)

docs.title: Decrypt
docs.text:
p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(enveloped)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
plaintext, err := p7.Decrypt(recipientCert, recipientKey, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("%s\n", plaintext)

Decrypt picks the recipient whose issuer and serial number match the certificate and fails with pkcs7: no enveloped recipient for provided certificate when there is none. It does not check that the key belongs to the certificate. A wrong key is treated like corrupted input, as Integrity describes.

The key transport is read from the message. PKCS #1 v1.5 and RSAES-OAEP are accepted. For RSAES-OAEP the hash, the MGF1 hash and the label come from the parameters. Absent parameters mean SHA-1 as RFC 8017 specifies.

docs.title: Accepted ciphers
docs.text:
Decrypt accepts AES-128-CBC, AES-192-CBC, AES-256-CBC and DES-EDE3-CBC by default, the list in DefaultContentDecryptionAlgorithms. A message encrypted with another cipher fails with an error that wraps ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed. DecryptOptions.ContentEncryptionAlgorithms replaces the list. Single DES must be listed explicitly:

_, err = p7.Decrypt(cert, key, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{})
fmt.Println("refused by default:", errors.Is(err, pkcs7.ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed))

opts := pkcs7.DecryptOptions{
    ContentEncryptionAlgorithms: append(slices.Clone(pkcs7.DefaultContentDecryptionAlgorithms), pkcs7.DESCBC),
}
plaintext, err := p7.Decrypt(cert, key, opts)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("%s\n", plaintext)

Accept DES-CBC only from peers that cannot do better. Its 56-bit key is broken.

Do not modify DefaultContentDecryptionAlgorithms itself. Every Decrypt and DecryptUsingPSK call reads it, so a change affects the whole program. Pass ContentEncryptionAlgorithms instead.

docs.title: Several keys
docs.text:
A receiver that holds several keys, for example during a key rollover, reads the recipients first and decrypts with the key that matches:

type candidate struct {
    cert *x509.Certificate
    key  crypto.Decrypter
}
candidates := []candidate{{currentCert, currentKey}, {nextCert, nextKey}}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(enveloped)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
recipients, err := p7.Recipients()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
for _, r := range recipients {
    for _, c := range candidates {
        if bytes.Equal(r.Issuer, c.cert.RawIssuer) && r.SerialNumber.Cmp(c.cert.SerialNumber) == 0 {
            plaintext, err := p7.Decrypt(c.cert, c.key, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{})
            if err != nil {
                log.Fatal(err)
            }
            fmt.Printf("%s with %s\n", plaintext, c.cert.Subject.CommonName)
        }
    }
}

Recipients lists them in encoded order. DER sorts the recipient set, so the order need not match the certificates given to Encrypt.

docs.title: Keys in an HSM
docs.text:
Decrypt takes a crypto.Decrypter, so the private key may stay in an HSM. The library calls its Decrypt method with these options:

  • *rsa.PKCS1v15DecryptOptions with SessionKeyLen set to the content key length, for PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport.
  • *rsa.OAEPOptions with Hash, MGFHash and Label from the message, for RSAES-OAEP.

The crypto.Decrypter must honor them. With SessionKeyLen set, *rsa.PrivateKey returns a random key of that length when the padding is wrong instead of an error, which is the RFC 3218 countermeasure against Bleichenbacher's attack. A crypto.Decrypter that returns an error instead still produces ErrDecryptionFailed, but whether it leaks timing then depends on that implementation.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every failure to decrypt the content key or the content returns ErrDecryptionFailed, without saying which step failed. That includes an error from the crypto.Decrypter, a content key of the wrong length and bad padding. A sender therefore cannot use the error as a padding oracle.

Other errors describe the message rather than the keys:

Error Cause ErrNotEncryptedContent The message is not EnvelopedData ErrUnsupportedAsymmetricEncryptionAlgorithm The recipient uses a key transport other than PKCS #1 v1.5 or RSAES-OAEP ErrUnsupportedAlgorithm The content cipher is not one this library implements ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed The content cipher is not in the accepted list pkcs7: encryption algorithm parameters are malformed The IV is missing or has the wrong length pkcs7: ciphertext is not a whole number of cipher blocks The ciphertext is truncated or empty

docs.title: Integrity
docs.text: CBC mode does not authenticate the content. A wrong key or a changed ciphertext usually ends in ErrDecryptionFailed, but sometimes the padding happens to be valid and Decrypt returns garbage. When the receiver must detect changes, sign the EnvelopedData message, as SCEP does.

docs.title: Parsing
docs.text: Parse decodes one CMS ContentInfo into a *PKCS7. It reads the structure only. Signatures, chains and CRLs are not checked until the caller asks for it.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Parse takes binary BER or DER. The input must hold exactly one ContentInfo with nothing after it. PEM, the form OpenSSL writes with -outform PEM, must be decoded first:

block, _ := pem.Decode(pemData)
if block == nil {
    log.Fatal("no PEM block found")
}
p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(block.Bytes)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println(len(p7.Certificates), "certificate and", len(p7.Signers), "signers")

pem.Decode ignores the block type, so it reads both the PKCS7 blocks of openssl smime and openssl pkcs7 and the CMS blocks of openssl cms.

docs.title: BER
docs.text:
OpenSSL with -stream and Apple App Attest receipts, among others, use BER indefinite lengths. Parse converts the input to DER lengths first and joins content that is split into several OCTET STRING segments. The conversion refuses input that is malformed or built to exhaust the parser:

  • nesting deeper than 64 levels
  • lengths longer than 4 octets or longer than the remaining data
  • indefinite lengths on primitive elements
  • end-of-contents octets outside an indefinite-length element
  • data after the message

docs.title: What Parse fills in
docs.text:
Content type Fields and methods SignedData Content, Certificates, CRLs and Signers. Then Verify, GetOnlySigner and UnmarshalSignedAttribute EnvelopedData No fields. Recipients, ContentEncryptionAlgorithm and Decrypt EncryptedData No fields. ContentEncryptionAlgorithm and DecryptUsingPSK

Any other content type fails with ErrUnsupportedContentType. An EnvelopedData message with a recipient type other than an RSA certificate identified by issuer and serial number fails to parse with an encoding/asn1 error.

Content holds the encapsulated content of a SignedData message. It is empty for a detached signature or a certificate bundle.

docs.title: Certificates and CRLs
docs.text:
The certificates in a SignedData message are parsed with crypto/x509. A certificate it refuses makes Parse fail. They are not checked further until Verify builds a chain.

Some Windows SCEP clients send certificates whose authority key identifier extension is marked critical, which RFC 5280 forbids and crypto/x509 refuses. With LegacyCertificateParser, ParseWithOptions then parses every certificate of the message again with a copy of the Go 1.23 parser that skips that check:

if _, err := pkcs7.Parse(request); err != nil {
    fmt.Println(err)
}
p7, err := pkcs7.ParseWithOptions(request, pkcs7.ParseOptions{LegacyCertificateParser: true})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println(p7.Certificates[0].Subject.CommonName)

The retry happens only for that one error. All certificates of such a message then come from the old parser, which gets no fixes from later Go releases. Enable the option only where those clients must be served.

CRLs holds the decoded revocation lists without any signature check. Encode one again and parse it with crypto/x509 to check it against the issuer:

message, err := pkcs7.DegenerateCRL(crlDER)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(message)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
raw, err := asn1.Marshal(p7.CRLs[0])
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
crl, err := x509.ParseRevocationList(raw)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := crl.CheckSignatureFrom(caCert); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println("CRL number", crl.Number)

A certificate bundle is read the same way through Certificates. Nothing in a bundle is signed, so treat its certificates as untrusted until a chain check accepts them.

docs.title: Pre-shared keys
docs.text:
An EncryptedData message carries content encrypted with a symmetric key that both sides already hold. The message names the cipher but not the key, so the parties agree on the key outside the message.

key := make([]byte, 32) // AES256CBC needs a 32-byte key
if _, err := rand.Read(key); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
opts := pkcs7.EncryptOptions{ContentEncryption: pkcs7.AES256CBC}
encrypted, err := pkcs7.EncryptUsingPSK([]byte("shared secret content"), key, opts)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(encrypted)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
plaintext, err := p7.DecryptUsingPSK(key, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("%s\n", plaintext)

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The key must have exactly the length the cipher needs:

ContentEncryption Key length AES128CBC, the default 16 bytes AES192CBC 24 bytes AES256CBC 32 bytes DESEDE3CBC 24 bytes DESCBC 8 bytes

EncryptUsingPSK fails with ErrPSKNotProvided for a nil key and with an error such as pkcs7: AES-256-CBC needs a 32-byte key, got 16 bytes for a key of the wrong length. DecryptUsingPSK returns the same length error. Use random key bytes, for example from crypto/rand. The library does not derive keys from passwords.

EncryptOptions.KeyEncryption and OAEPHash have no effect here.

docs.title: Decryption
docs.text:
DecryptUsingPSK takes the same DecryptOptions as Decrypt, so DES-CBC is refused unless it is listed. It returns ErrNotEncryptedContent for a message that is not EncryptedData and ErrDecryptionFailed when the padding is wrong.

As with EnvelopedData, CBC mode does not authenticate the content. A wrong key or a changed ciphertext usually fails with ErrDecryptionFailed but can also yield garbage. Sign the message when the receiver must detect changes.

docs.title: OpenSSL
docs.text: OpenSSL reads and writes these messages with openssl cms -EncryptedData_decrypt and -EncryptedData_encrypt, with the key given in hex through -secretkey. OpenSSL lists the tested commands.

docs.title: Signing
docs.text: A SignedData message carries content, one or more signatures over it and usually the certificates a receiver needs to check them. This page builds such messages and the certificate and CRL bundles that use the same structure without signers.

docs.title: Sign content
docs.text:
sd, err := pkcs7.NewSignedData([]byte("hello, CMS"))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := sd.AddSigner(cert, key, pkcs7.SignerInfoConfig{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
signed, err := sd.Finish()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

NewSignedData takes the content. AddSigner adds one signer with its certificate, its private key and a SignerInfoConfig. Finish returns the encoded ContentInfo. Every message this library signs has the encapsulated content type id-data.

docs.title: Signer keys
docs.text:
The key is a crypto.Signer whose public key is an *rsa.PublicKey or an *ecdsa.PublicKey. Any other key type fails with pkcs7: unsupported signer key type. The library hashes the data and calls Sign with the digest and the hash as options:

  • For RSA it expects a PKCS #1 v1.5 signature, which *rsa.PrivateKey returns for these options. RSASSA-PSS signing is not supported.
  • For ECDSA it expects the ASN.1 encoded signature that *ecdsa.PrivateKey returns.

A key held in an HSM or a remote signing service works when its crypto.Signer follows the same contract. The library does not check that the key matches the certificate, so a mismatch shows up only when the message is verified.

docs.title: Digest algorithm
docs.text:
Signers use SHA-256 unless SetDigestAlgorithm names another digest. The setting applies to signers added after the call, so each signer of one message may use a different digest. For example, sd.SetDigestAlgorithm(pkcs7.OIDDigestAlgorithmSHA384) selects SHA-384.

RSA signers accept MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. ECDSA signers accept SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. Another combination fails when the signer is added. MD5 and SHA-1 remain available for old peers, but Verify refuses MD5 unless the receiver allows it.

docs.title: Signature algorithm identifier
docs.text: The signer info names the signature algorithm. By default it is derived from the key and the digest, for example sha256WithRSAEncryption or ecdsa-with-SHA256. Some peers expect the plain rsaEncryption identifier for RSA signatures, which is also what OpenSSL writes. sd.SetEncryptionAlgorithm(pkcs7.OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSA) selects it for signers added afterwards. Any other value must equal the derived identifier. Otherwise AddSigner fails.

docs.title: Signed attributes
docs.text:
AddSigner signs a set of attributes rather than the content itself. The set always holds:

  • content-type, with the value id-data
  • message-digest, the digest of the content
  • signing-time, the current time or SignerInfoConfig.SigningTime, stored in UTC

SignerInfoConfig.ExtraSignedAttributes adds more. ExtraUnsignedAttributes adds attributes outside the signature. Each Attribute value must be encodable by encoding/asn1. The set is sorted into DER order before it is signed. The receiver reads an attribute back with UnmarshalSignedAttribute after verifying the message:

// An attribute type from a private arc. Use the OID your protocol defines.
oidTransactionID := asn1.ObjectIdentifier{1, 3, 6, 1, 4, 1, 99999, 1}

sd, err := pkcs7.NewSignedData([]byte("content"))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
config := pkcs7.SignerInfoConfig{
    ExtraSignedAttributes: []pkcs7.Attribute{
        {Type: oidTransactionID, Value: "transaction-42"},
    },
}
if err := sd.AddSigner(cert, key, config); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
signed, err := sd.Finish()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(signed)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
var transactionID string
if err := p7.UnmarshalSignedAttribute(oidTransactionID, &transactionID); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println(transactionID)

Do not put content-type, message-digest or signing-time into ExtraSignedAttributes. AddSigner accepts the duplicate, but Verify then fails because each of them must appear only once.

GetSignedData returns the structure being built. The SetUnauthenticatedAttributes method of an entry in its SignerInfos replaces the unsigned attributes of a signer that is already added, for example sd.GetSignedData().SignerInfos[0].SetUnauthenticatedAttributes(attrs). The signature does not cover them, so it stays valid.

docs.title: Certificate chains
docs.text:
AddSigner puts the signer certificate into the message. AddSignerChain also adds the issuing CA certificates, so a receiver that trusts only the root can build the chain:

sd, err := pkcs7.NewSignedData([]byte("signed through an intermediate"))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
parents := []*x509.Certificate{intermediateCert}
if err := sd.AddSignerChain(cert, key, parents, pkcs7.SignerInfoConfig{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
signed, err := sd.Finish()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(signed)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
roots := x509.NewCertPool()
roots.AddCert(rootCert)
if err := p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{Roots: roots}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println(len(p7.Certificates), "certificates in the message")

List the parents in order, starting with the issuer of the signer certificate. AddSignerChain checks that each certificate is signed by the next one and fails otherwise. It does not require the last parent to be a root. AddCertificate adds any other certificate to the message.

docs.title: Messages without certificates
docs.text:
RFC 5652 allows a message without certificates when the receiver already holds the signer certificate. SCEP clients, for example, have the CA certificate from GetCACert. RemoveCertificates leaves out every certificate added so far:

sd, err := pkcs7.NewSignedData([]byte("no certificates attached"))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := sd.AddSigner(cert, key, pkcs7.SignerInfoConfig{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
sd.RemoveCertificates()
signed, err := sd.Finish()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(signed)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
opts := pkcs7.VerifyOptions{SignerCertificates: []*x509.Certificate{cert}}
if err := p7.Verify(opts); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println("verified with a known signer certificate")

Call it after the last AddSigner, because signers added later put their certificates back. The receiver passes the expected signer certificate in VerifyOptions.SignerCertificates.

docs.title: Detached signatures
docs.text:
A detached signature leaves the content out of the message. The receiver gets the content another way and sets p7.Content before calling Verify:

content := []byte("content sent next to the signature")
sd, err := pkcs7.NewSignedData(content)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := sd.AddSigner(cert, key, pkcs7.SignerInfoConfig{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
sd.Detach()
signature, err := sd.Finish()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(signature)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println("content in the message:", len(p7.Content))
p7.Content = content
if err := p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println("detached signature verified")

Call Detach after the signers are added and right before Finish.

docs.title: Several signers
docs.text: Call AddSigner once per signer. Each signer has its own certificate, digest and attributes. Verify requires every signature to be valid.

docs.title: Signatures without signed attributes
docs.text:
SignWithoutAttr signs the digest of the content directly, without signed attributes. Old Android APK signatures use this form. It ignores its SignerInfoConfig.

RemoveAuthenticatedAttributes deletes the signed attributes from signers that already exist. Their signatures cover those attributes, so the resulting message fails verification in this library and in OpenSSL. Use SignWithoutAttr to build a message without signed attributes. RemoveUnauthenticatedAttributes deletes the unsigned attributes, which the signatures do not cover.

docs.title: Certificate and CRL bundles
docs.text:
A SignedData message without signers is a common way to ship certificates, as in a .p7b file or an EST or SCEP certificate response. DegenerateCertificate takes one or more DER certificates concatenated into one byte slice:

var chain []byte
for _, cert := range []*x509.Certificate{leaf, intermediate.cert} {
    chain = append(chain, cert.Raw...)
}
bundle, err := pkcs7.DegenerateCertificate(chain)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(bundle)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
for _, cert := range p7.Certificates {
    fmt.Println(cert.Subject.CommonName)
}

It does not parse the certificates, so check them before building the bundle.

DegenerateCRL wraps one DER encoded CRL, the form of a SCEP GetCRL response. It fails when the input is not a single well-formed CRL structure. It does not check the CRL signature. Parsing shows how a receiver checks it.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Verify checks the signers of a parsed SignedData message. Parsing alone checks nothing, so call Verify before using the content or the signed attributes.

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(signed)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
roots := x509.NewCertPool()
roots.AddCert(caCert)
if err := p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{Roots: roots}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("%s\n", p7.Content)

docs.title: What Verify checks
docs.text:
Verify fails when the message has no signers. Otherwise it checks every signer and returns the first failure, so a message is accepted only when all of its signatures are valid. For each signer it:

  1. Finds the signer certificate by issuer and serial number, first among the certificates in the message and then in VerifyOptions.SignerCertificates.
  2. Refuses the MD5 digest unless VerifyOptions.AllowMD5 is set.
  3. When the signer has signed attributes, requires exactly one content-type attribute equal to the encapsulated content type and exactly one message-digest attribute equal to the digest of p7.Content. A signing-time attribute, when present, must fall within the validity of the signer certificate.
  4. Checks the signature over the signed attributes as they were received. A signer without signed attributes signs the content itself. The signature algorithm must suit the key and the digest.
  5. When VerifyOptions.Roots is set, builds a chain from the signer certificate to one of the roots.

Without Roots, step 5 is skipped. The signatures are then known to come from the keys of the certificates the message names, but nothing says those certificates are trustworthy. Set Roots unless the caller checks the signer certificate itself, for example by comparing it with a certificate it already holds.

docs.title: Trust anchors and intermediates
docs.text:
The chain is built with crypto/x509 from the signer certificate through the certificates in the message and VerifyOptions.Intermediates to a certificate in Roots. A CA that does not send its intermediates can still be verified when the receiver supplies them in Intermediates.

KeyUsages lists the extended key usages to accept, for example []x509.ExtKeyUsage{x509.ExtKeyUsageEmailProtection}. The chain passes when it allows at least one of them. When the list is empty, any usage is accepted. crypto/x509 treats a certificate without an extended key usage extension as valid for any usage.

Chain errors wrap the crypto/x509 error, so errors.As finds an x509.CertificateInvalidError or an x509.UnknownAuthorityError.

docs.title: Check time
docs.text:
The chain is checked at the current time by default. Two options change that:

  • CurrentTime checks the chain at a fixed time.
  • VerifyAtSigningTime checks it at the time in the signing-time attribute when CurrentTime is zero. A signer without that attribute is checked at the current time.

The signer chooses the signing time, so it proves nothing about when the signature was made. Use VerifyAtSigningTime only for archived signatures whose signing time you have reason to trust, such as documents you stored yourself:

if err := p7.Verify(pkcs7.VerifyOptions{Roots: roots}); err != nil {
    var invalid x509.CertificateInvalidError
    fmt.Println("expired now:", errors.As(err, &invalid) && invalid.Reason == x509.Expired)
}
opts := pkcs7.VerifyOptions{Roots: roots, VerifyAtSigningTime: true}
if err := p7.Verify(opts); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println("verified at the signing time")

The signing time is always compared with the signer certificate validity, with or without Roots. A signing time outside it fails with a *SigningTimeNotValidError.

docs.title: Detached content
docs.text: A detached signature carries no content, so p7.Content is empty after Parse. Set it to the signed bytes before calling Verify, as Signing shows. The bytes must match exactly. OpenSSL, for example, converts line endings to CRLF when it signs without -binary.

docs.title: Signer certificates outside the message
docs.text:
Some SCEP servers answer without their signer certificate. The receiver passes the certificate it expects in SignerCertificates:

sd, err := pkcs7.NewSignedData([]byte("no certificates attached"))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := sd.AddSigner(cert, key, pkcs7.SignerInfoConfig{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
sd.RemoveCertificates()
signed, err := sd.Finish()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

p7, err := pkcs7.Parse(signed)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
opts := pkcs7.VerifyOptions{SignerCertificates: []*x509.Certificate{cert}}
if err := p7.Verify(opts); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println("verified with a known signer certificate")

A certificate in SignerCertificates is used only when the message does not carry a certificate with the same issuer and serial number. It still goes through the chain check when Roots is set.

docs.title: Reading signer information
docs.text:
• p7.Signers holds the parsed signer infos. Its length is the number of signers.
  • GetOnlySigner returns the signer certificate when the message has exactly one signer and carries its certificate. It returns nil otherwise.
  • UnmarshalSignedAttribute decodes a signed attribute of the first signer. The attribute must appear once with a single value. It returns ErrAttributeNotFound when the attribute is absent. Signing shows an example.

docs.title: Custom hashing
docs.text: p7.Hasher replaces the standard library hash when Verify computes the content digest for the message-digest attribute. It does not apply to the hash of the signed attributes or to signers without signed attributes.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Error Cause *MessageDigestMismatchError The content does not match the message-digest attribute. The content was changed or a detached signature was given the wrong bytes *SigningTimeNotValidError The signing time is outside the signer certificate validity pkcs7: no certificate for signer Neither the message nor SignerCertificates holds the signer certificate pkcs7: signer uses the MD5 digest, which is not allowed The signer uses MD5 and AllowMD5 is not set pkcs7: failed to verify certificate chain: ... The chain to Roots cannot be built at the check time or allows none of the usages in KeyUsages

Errors lists more errors and how to compare them.

docs.title: OpenSSL
docs.text: The tests exchange messages with the openssl command found on the PATH. They skip when it is missing, so run make test TESTFLAGS=-v to see whether they ran. They pass with OpenSSL 3.0 and 4.1. This page lists only what those tests check.

docs.title: Messages this library creates
docs.text:
Message OpenSSL command Test SignedData from RSA and ECDSA P-256 signers with SHA-256, attached openssl cms -verify -binary -inform DER -in signed.der -CAfile root.pem TestOpenSSLVerifiesSignedData The same, detached The same with -content content.txt TestOpenSSLVerifiesSignedData The same, without signed attributes (SignWithoutAttr) The same as attached TestOpenSSLVerifiesSignedData EnvelopedData with AES-256-CBC and PKCS #1 v1.5, AES-128-CBC and RSAES-OAEP SHA-256, DES-EDE3-CBC and RSAES-OAEP SHA-512 openssl cms -decrypt -inform PEM -in enveloped.pem -recip recipient.pem, where recipient.pem holds the certificate and the key TestEncryptAndDecryptWithOpenSSL EncryptedData with AES-128-CBC, AES-192-CBC, AES-256-CBC and DES-EDE3-CBC openssl cms -EncryptedData_decrypt -inform DER -in encrypted.der -secretkey <hex key> TestEncryptUsingPSKWithOpenSSL Certificate bundle from DegenerateCertificate and CRL message from DegenerateCRL openssl pkcs7 -inform DER -in bundle.p7b TestDegenerateCertificate, TestDegenerateCRL

OpenSSL accepts every message. Where a message carries content, the tests compare what OpenSSL returns with the original.

docs.title: Messages OpenSSL creates
docs.text:
OpenSSL command Library call Test openssl smime -sign -nodetach -signer signer.pem -inkey signer.key -certfile intermediate.pem -outform PEM with RSA 2048 and 4096 and ECDSA P-256, P-384 and P-521 keys in every root, intermediate and signer combination Verify with the root in Roots TestSignWithOpenSSLAndVerify openssl cms -sign -binary -nodetach -md sha256 -keyopt rsa_padding_mode:pss -keyopt rsa_pss_saltlen:digest, also with -md sha384 and with a salt length of 20 Verify TestVerifyRSAPSSFromOpenSSL openssl cms -EncryptedData_encrypt -binary -aes128 -secretkey <hex key> -outform DER, also with -aes192, -aes256 and -des3 DecryptUsingPSK TestEncryptUsingPSKWithOpenSSL openssl cms -encrypt -binary -aes128 -keyopt rsa_padding_mode:oaep -keyopt rsa_oaep_md:sha256 -keyopt rsa_mgf1_md:sha1 -keyopt rsa_oaep_label:0102030405, also with rsa_mgf1_md:sha512 Decrypt TestDecryptOpenSSLOAEPParameters

TestDecrypt also decrypts four EnvelopedData messages that OpenSSL produced when the tests were written. They are stored in decrypt_test.go with the commands that made them:

Command Content cipher Key transport openssl cms -encrypt -in test.txt cert.pem DES-EDE3-CBC PKCS #1 v1.5 openssl smime -encrypt -in test.txt -aes256 -outform pem certificate.pem AES-256-CBC PKCS #1 v1.5 openssl cms -encrypt ... -aes256 -keyopt rsa_padding_mode:oaep AES-256-CBC RSAES-OAEP with SHA-1 The same with -keyopt rsa_oaep_md:sha256 AES-256-CBC RSAES-OAEP with SHA-256

docs.title: Line endings
docs.text: OpenSSL treats the input as text unless -binary is given and converts line endings to CRLF before signing. The signed content then differs from the file on disk, so a detached signature made that way verifies only against the converted bytes. The tests pass -binary when they sign with openssl cms.

docs.title: What OpenSSL can produce but this library cannot read
docs.text: OpenSSL also writes structures outside the Support matrix, such as recipients identified by subject key identifier (-keyid), AES-GCM content in AuthEnvelopedData and recipients with EC keys. Known limitations lists them.

docs.title: Content ciphers
docs.text:
ContentEncryptionAlgorithm selects the symmetric cipher of EnvelopedData and EncryptedData content. Its zero value selects AES128CBC. String returns the name in the second column.

Constant Name OID variable Key length AES128CBC AES-128-CBC OIDEncryptionAlgorithmAES128CBC (2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1.2) 16 bytes AES192CBC AES-192-CBC OIDEncryptionAlgorithmAES192CBC (2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1.22) 24 bytes AES256CBC AES-256-CBC OIDEncryptionAlgorithmAES256CBC (2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1.42) 32 bytes DESEDE3CBC DES-EDE3-CBC OIDEncryptionAlgorithmDESEDE3CBC (1.2.840.113549.3.7) 24 bytes DESCBC DES-CBC OIDEncryptionAlgorithmDESCBC (1.3.14.3.2.7) 8 bytes

Every cipher runs in CBC mode with PKCS #7 padding and a random IV, which the algorithm parameter carries. DefaultContentDecryptionAlgorithms lists the ciphers decryption accepts by default, all of these except DESCBC.

docs.title: Key transport
docs.text:
KeyEncryptionAlgorithm selects how Encrypt protects the content key for each recipient. Its zero value selects RSAPKCS1v15.

Constant Name OID variable RSAPKCS1v15 RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5 OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSA (1.2.840.113549.1.1.1) RSAOAEP RSAES-OAEP OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSAESOAEP (1.2.840.113549.1.1.7)

RSAES-OAEP parameters use OIDMaskGenerationFunctionMGF1 (1.2.840.113549.1.1.8) and, when a message carries a label, OIDOAEPSourcePSpecified (1.2.840.113549.1.1.9).

docs.text:
OID variable Digest OID OIDDigestAlgorithmMD5 MD5 1.2.840.113549.2.5 OIDDigestAlgorithmSHA1 SHA-1 1.3.14.3.2.26 OIDDigestAlgorithmSHA224 SHA-224 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.4 OIDDigestAlgorithmSHA256 SHA-256, the signing default 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.1 OIDDigestAlgorithmSHA384 SHA-384 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.2 OIDDigestAlgorithmSHA512 SHA-512 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.3

Some signers, such as the Azure instance metadata attestation service, put an RSA signature algorithm identifier in the digest algorithm field. Verify accepts that and uses its hash.

docs.title: Signature algorithms
docs.text:
RSA PKCS #1 v1.5:

OID variable Algorithm OID OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSA rsaEncryption, with any digest 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1 OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSAMD5 md5WithRSAEncryption 1.2.840.113549.1.1.4 OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSASHA1 sha1WithRSAEncryption 1.2.840.113549.1.1.5 OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSASHA224 sha224WithRSAEncryption 1.2.840.113549.1.1.14 OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSASHA256 sha256WithRSAEncryption 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSASHA384 sha384WithRSAEncryption 1.2.840.113549.1.1.12 OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSASHA512 sha512WithRSAEncryption 1.2.840.113549.1.1.13

OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSASSAPSS (1.2.840.113549.1.1.10) is RSASSA-PSS. Verify accepts it when its parameters are present, their hash and MGF1 hash both equal the signer digest, the trailer field is 1 and the salt length is not negative. The library does not sign with it.

ECDSA:

OID variable Algorithm OID OIDDigestAlgorithmECDSASHA1 ecdsa-with-SHA1 1.2.840.10045.4.1 OIDDigestAlgorithmECDSASHA256 ecdsa-with-SHA256 1.2.840.10045.4.3.2 OIDDigestAlgorithmECDSASHA384 ecdsa-with-SHA384 1.2.840.10045.4.3.3 OIDDigestAlgorithmECDSASHA512 ecdsa-with-SHA512 1.2.840.10045.4.3.4

Despite the OIDDigestAlgorithm prefix these are signature algorithm identifiers. The curve identifiers OIDEncryptionAlgorithmECDSAP256 (1.2.840.10045.3.1.7), OIDEncryptionAlgorithmECDSAP384 (1.3.132.0.34) and OIDEncryptionAlgorithmECDSAP521 (1.3.132.0.35) are accepted in the signature algorithm field when verifying, because some signers write them there. They are never written.

When signing, the identifier is derived from the key and the digest:

Key Digest Identifier written RSA MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 The matching sha*WithRSAEncryption. rsaEncryption after SetEncryptionAlgorithm(OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSA) ECDSA SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 The matching ecdsa-with-SHA*

The OID variables are exported so callers can compare against them. Do not modify them, because the library reads the same variables.

docs.title: Compatibility policy
docs.text: The module uses semantic versioning. The public API is every exported identifier of the package pkcs7. The packages under internal/ are not part of it and cannot be imported from other modules.

docs.title: Before v1.0.0
docs.text: A minor release may change the public API. The changelog describes every change that affects callers, including any that needs a code change.

docs.title: Rules for every release
docs.text:
• Option structs may gain fields. Construct SignerInfoConfig, VerifyOptions, EncryptOptions, DecryptOptions and ParseOptions with field names.
  • Constants may be added. A switch over ContentEncryptionAlgorithm or KeyEncryptionAlgorithm needs a default case.
  • Parsing and verification may become stricter when a message breaks RFC 5652 or a related RFC. The changelog names such a change.
  • Error texts may change. Compare errors with errors.Is and errors.As, as Errors describes.
  • Defaults may change in a minor release. The changelog names the change. Version 0.3.0, for example, moved signing from SHA-1 to SHA-256 and encryption from DES-CBC to AES-128-CBC.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
1. Read the changelog section for the new version.
  2. Run go get github.com/misiektoja/go-pkcs7@vX.Y.Z and build.
  3. Run your tests against the peers you exchange messages with.

docs.title: Go version
docs.text: The module declares its minimum Go version in go.mod, currently Go 1.27.3. CI builds and tests with exactly that version. The changelog names every change of the minimum.

docs.title: Module path and older tags
docs.text: The module path is github.com/misiektoja/go-pkcs7. Releases of smallstep/pkcs7 up to v0.2.3 use another module path and are not versions of this module. Migrating from smallstep/pkcs7 lists the changes.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Compare errors with errors.Is and errors.As, not by their text. Some sentinel errors are returned wrapped. The texts of other errors may change in any release.

docs.text:
Error Returned by Meaning ErrUnsupportedContentType Parse, ParseWithOptions The content type is not SignedData, EnvelopedData or EncryptedData ErrAttributeNotFound UnmarshalSignedAttribute, Verify The first signer has no signed attribute of that type. Verify returns it wrapped when a signer lacks the content-type or message-digest attribute ErrUnsupportedEncryptionAlgorithm Encrypt, EncryptUsingPSK EncryptOptions.ContentEncryption is not a known constant ErrUnsupportedKeyEncryptionAlgorithm Encrypt EncryptOptions.KeyEncryption is not a known constant ErrUnsupportedKeyEncryptionHash Encrypt EncryptOptions.OAEPHash is not SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 ErrUnsupportedKeyType Encrypt A recipient certificate does not hold an RSA key ErrPSKNotProvided EncryptUsingPSK The key is nil ErrNotEncryptedContent Decrypt, DecryptUsingPSK, Recipients, ContentEncryptionAlgorithm The message is not of the content type the method needs ErrUnsupportedAlgorithm Decrypt, DecryptUsingPSK, ContentEncryptionAlgorithm The content cipher is not one this library implements ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed Decrypt, DecryptUsingPSK The content cipher is not in DecryptOptions.ContentEncryptionAlgorithms. Returned wrapped with the cipher name ErrUnsupportedAsymmetricEncryptionAlgorithm Decrypt The recipient uses a key transport other than PKCS #1 v1.5 or RSAES-OAEP ErrDecryptionFailed Decrypt, DecryptUsingPSK The content key or the content could not be decrypted

ErrDecryptionFailed covers every failure that depends on the key: an error from the crypto.Decrypter, a content key of the wrong length and bad padding. It does not say which one happened, so a sender cannot use it as a padding oracle.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Every algorithm choice and every relaxation is made per call through these structs. Their zero values select the defaults listed here. Construct them with field names, because new fields may be added, as the Compatibility policy describes.

docs.title: SignerInfoConfig
docs.text:
Passed to AddSigner, AddSignerChain and SignWithoutAttr. SignWithoutAttr ignores it.

Field Type Default Meaning ExtraSignedAttributes []Attribute none Signed attributes added after content-type, message-digest and signing-time ExtraUnsignedAttributes []Attribute none Attributes outside the signature SigningTime time.Time the current time Value of the signing-time attribute, stored in UTC

Attribute has a Type (an asn1.ObjectIdentifier) and a Value that encoding/asn1 must be able to encode.

docs.title: SignedData settings
docs.text:
Two methods on SignedData apply to the signers added after the call:

Method Default Meaning SetDigestAlgorithm(oid) OIDDigestAlgorithmSHA256 Digest of the content and the signed attributes SetEncryptionAlgorithm(oid) derived from the key and the digest Signature algorithm identifier. For RSA keys OIDEncryptionAlgorithmRSA is also accepted. Any other value must equal the derived one

docs.title: VerifyOptions
docs.text:
Passed to Verify.

Field Type Default Meaning Roots *x509.CertPool nil, no chain check Trust anchors for the signer certificate chains Intermediates []*x509.Certificate none Certificates that may complete a chain, in addition to those in the message SignerCertificates []*x509.Certificate none Signer certificates for messages that do not carry them CurrentTime time.Time the current time Time at which chains are checked VerifyAtSigningTime bool false Check chains at the signing-time attribute when CurrentTime is zero KeyUsages []x509.ExtKeyUsage any usage Extended key usages to accept. The chain must allow at least one of them AllowMD5 bool false Accept signers that use the MD5 digest

Intermediates, CurrentTime, VerifyAtSigningTime and KeyUsages matter only when Roots is set. Verification explains each check.

docs.title: EncryptOptions
docs.text:
Passed to Encrypt and EncryptUsingPSK.

Field Type Default Meaning ContentEncryption ContentEncryptionAlgorithm AES128CBC Content cipher KeyEncryption KeyEncryptionAlgorithm RSAPKCS1v15 Key transport for each recipient. EncryptUsingPSK ignores it OAEPHash crypto.Hash crypto.SHA256 RSAES-OAEP hash and MGF1 hash. Used only with RSAOAEP

OAEPHash accepts crypto.SHA1, crypto.SHA224, crypto.SHA256, crypto.SHA384 and crypto.SHA512. Another value fails with ErrUnsupportedKeyEncryptionHash.

docs.title: DecryptOptions
docs.text:
Passed to Decrypt and DecryptUsingPSK.

Field Type Default Meaning ContentEncryptionAlgorithms []ContentEncryptionAlgorithm DefaultContentDecryptionAlgorithms Content ciphers to accept

DefaultContentDecryptionAlgorithms is AES128CBC, AES192CBC, AES256CBC and DESEDE3CBC. A non-empty list replaces it, so add the defaults to the list when extending it, as Encryption and decryption shows. The key transport is read from the message and needs no option.

DefaultContentDecryptionAlgorithms is an exported variable that every Decrypt and DecryptUsingPSK call reads. Do not modify it. Pass ContentEncryptionAlgorithms instead.

docs.title: ParseOptions
docs.text:
Passed to ParseWithOptions. Parse uses the zero value.

Field Type Default Meaning LegacyCertificateParser bool false When crypto/x509 refuses a certificate because its authority key identifier is marked critical, parse every certificate of the message again with a copy of the Go 1.23 parser

docs.title: PKCS7.Hasher
docs.text: A parsed message has a Hasher field. When it is set, Verify calls its Hash(crypto.Hash, io.Reader) ([]byte, error) method to compute the content digest that the message-digest attribute is compared with. It is nil by default, which uses the standard library hash.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text: This page states what the library guarantees, what it leaves to the caller and how it treats hostile input. Report a suspected vulnerability as the security policy describes.

docs.title: What a successful Verify means
docs.text:
When Verify returns nil, every signer of the message passed these checks:

  • The signature is valid for the public key in the signer certificate, with a signature algorithm that suits the key type and the digest.
  • With signed attributes, the message-digest attribute equals the digest of p7.Content and the content-type attribute equals the encapsulated content type. Each appears exactly once. The digests are compared in constant time.
  • A signing-time attribute, when present, falls within the signer certificate validity.
  • When VerifyOptions.Roots is set, crypto/x509 built a chain from the signer certificate to a root at the check time and the chain allows at least one of the extended key usages in KeyUsages.

docs.title: What the caller decides
docs.text:
• Trust. Without Roots no chain is built. The caller must then decide whether the signer certificate is acceptable, for example by comparing it with a certificate it already holds.
  • Revocation. Verify does not consult CRLs or OCSP. CRLs carried in a message are returned without any check.
  • Key usage. Verify checks extended key usages only through KeyUsages. It does not check the key usage extension or certificate policies of the signer certificate.
  • Signing time. The signer chooses the signing-time value. VerifyAtSigningTime should be used only when that time is trusted for another reason.
  • Recipients. Encrypt does not check the validity or the key usage of recipient certificates.
  • Input size. The library holds the whole message in memory and does not limit its size. Bound the input before calling Parse, for example with http.MaxBytesReader for an HTTP body.

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text:
The defaults avoid broken algorithms. Each relaxation is an option on the call that needs it.

Algorithm Default behavior MD5 digest Refused by Verify unless AllowMD5 is set. Signing with it requires SetDigestAlgorithm SHA-1 digest Accepted by Verify. Signing with it requires SetDigestAlgorithm DES-CBC content Refused by Decrypt and DecryptUsingPSK unless listed in DecryptOptions. Encryption with it requires EncryptOptions DES-EDE3-CBC content Accepted by Decrypt and DecryptUsingPSK PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport The default for Encrypt because SCEP peers expect it. Accepted by Decrypt with the countermeasure below

docs.title: Decryption failures
docs.text:
PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport is open to Bleichenbacher's padding oracle attack when a receiver reveals whether the padding was valid. Decrypt applies the RFC 3218 countermeasure. It asks the key for a random content key of the right length when the padding is bad and then continues as it would with any wrong key. Every failure to decrypt the content key or the content returns the same ErrDecryptionFailed. The content padding is removed in constant time.

A crypto.Decrypter other than *rsa.PrivateKey receives *rsa.PKCS1v15DecryptOptions with SessionKeyLen set and must implement the countermeasure itself to be safe.

docs.title: Confidentiality without integrity
docs.text: EnvelopedData and EncryptedData use CBC mode, which hides the content but does not authenticate it. A changed ciphertext or a wrong key is usually reported as ErrDecryptionFailed but can also decrypt to garbage. Sign the message when the receiver must detect changes. AuthEnvelopedData with AES-GCM is not supported.

docs.title: Hostile input
docs.text:
Parse accepts input from untrusted peers. The BER converter refuses nesting deeper than 64 levels, lengths longer than four octets or beyond the end of the input, indefinite lengths on primitive elements, stray end-of-contents octets and trailing data.

Two fuzz targets cover this code. FuzzBer2Der checks that the converter never panics and that its output converts to itself. FuzzParse checks that parsing, verification and decryption of arbitrary input return errors instead of panicking. CI runs each for 30 seconds on every push and pull request to dev and main.

docs.title: Certificates
docs.text: Embedded certificates are parsed by crypto/x509. One it refuses makes Parse fail. ParseOptions.LegacyCertificateParser acts only when crypto/x509 refuses a certificate because its authority key identifier is marked critical. It then parses every certificate of the message again with a copy of the Go 1.23 parser, not only the refused one. That copy lives under internal/legacy/x509 and gets no fixes from later Go releases, so enable the option only where the Windows SCEP clients that need it must be served.

docs.title: Randomness
docs.text: Content keys, IVs, RSA encryption padding and signatures use crypto/rand.
